newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar whipsaws after U.S., German jobs data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar whipsaws after U.S., German jobs data.

text.p: The dollar briefly soared above 1.74 marks to a 39-month high on Friday after jobs reports in the United States and Germany showed the sharply divergent prospects of the two economic powerhouses.

The U.S. currency, already buoyant after a gloomy German job report, leapt to a high of 1.7423 marks when key U.S. non-farm payrolls figures for May underlined the strength of the American economy. It then beat a retreat on profit-taking.

The U.S. jobless rate unexpectedly fell to 4.8 percent in May, its lowest level since October 1973, while figures from the German Bundesbank showed 11.4 percent of Germans were out of work in May based on adjusted data, compared with 11.2 percent in April.
Wall Street opened strongly, despite predictions, putting on more than 30 points in the first 30 minutes of trading.
Even the German market jumped to a new trading high in bourse trade and responded positively in post-bourse trading to the strength of the dollar and U.S. data.
The rest of Europe's main bourses also had a good day, with London advancing one percent, despite the Bank of England raising bank base rates by a quarter point to 6.5 percent.
Bond markets wobbled but then steadied after the U.S. figures initially spooked traders by showing jobs growth slowed sharply in May although earlier months were revised upwards significantly.
Precious metals palladium and platinum, which have soared in recent days because of delays in Russian exports, pushed sharply higher again during the morning.
Platinum zoomed $60 to $495 an ounce to its highest level since 1990. Palladium, which fixed at a 17-year high of $240.00 in the morning, was trading at $225.00 in the afternoon.

The German jobs figures, which showed a seasonally adjusted rise of 56,000 in the number of people out of work to 4.358 million, intensified concerns over how Bonn could cut its budget deficit to the 3.0 percent of GDP required for the European single currency.

"The German jobless numbers are making people ask what Kohl and Waigel are going to do about their budget problems and make them more inclined to hold long dollar positions," said Chris Tinker, chief treasury economist at Standard Chartered."

German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and his embattled finance minister Theo Waigel have repeatedly declared their commitment to meeting strict criteria for economic and monetary unilon (EMU), despite Germany's sizeable budget shortfall.
The foreign exchange market responded by pushing the dollar higher, and piled into dollars even more after the U.S. report before profit-taking and talk of central bank offers prompted a retreat.
By 1415 GMT the dollar stood at 1.7341 marks, up from late Thursday's 1.7285. Against the yen the dollar stood at 115.61 versus 115.65.

Despite gloomy comments from German officials at the prospects of a revival in the jobs market, the country's share market remained strong although it closed off its intraday record of 3,708.25 at 3,695.29, up 0.61 percent.
In later screen-based trade the IBIS-DAX index climbed back through 3,700, only to beat a retreat to around 3,687.
SGL Carbon , which closed bourse trade down 21.2 marks at 239, recovered later after the company denied involvement in allegations of graphite electrode price fixing.
British shares firmed to their best levels for the day after the U.S. data and bond markets steadied. By 1415 GMT the FTSE 100 was up just over one percent at 4,626 points.
Bank shares, already up amid renewed bid speculation, added to their gains after the interest rate hike, which the market saw as a sign that the central bank was acting positively.
Shares in National Westminster Bank led the sector wide rally, rising 45p to 781, on talk of a merger with Abbey National, which added 9p to 852.5.
French shares initally retreated after the U.S. data unsettled bonds but the blue chip CAC-40 later recovered to stand around 19 points higher by late afternoon in Paris.
Analysts said jobs data showed the strength of the U.S. economy, fuelling prospects of an American rate hike.
Retailer Pinault-Printemps shades back from highs but was still up 3.50 percent at 2,630 francs after reporting sales to the end of May up 7.6 percent.
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7341 marks and 115.61 yen compared with 1.7285 marks and 115.65 yen in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1415 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 50.1 points, or 1.09 percent, at 4,626.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 19.4 points, or 0.72 percent, at 2,710.25.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 22.26 points, or 0.61 percent, at 3,695.29. In later screen trade, the IBIS-DAX index was up three at 3,687.05
PRECIOUS METALS
Platinum rose to $495.00 from $435.00 in themorning, while palladium advanced to $225.00 from $210.00.
Gold fixed at $344.00, up 20 cents, while silver was up 11 cents at $4.91.
